entries.name: Partial<T>
entries.description: Constructs a type with all properties of T set to optional. Useful for update payloads and partial configuration objects.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The type whose properties to make optional.

examples.title: Partial update type
Default config merging

bestPractices: Combine with Required<> for validation after merge

entries.name: Required<T>
entries.description: Constructs a type with all properties of T set to required (non-optional). Opposite of Partial<T>.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The type whose optional properties to make required.

examples.title: Require all config fields

useCases: Ensuring all config options are provided
POST request bodies where all fields are mandatory

entries.name: Readonly<T>
entries.description: Constructs a type with all properties of T set to readonly. Prevents property reassignment at the type level.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The type whose properties to make readonly.

examples.title: Immutable state
Readonly function parameter

commonMistakes: Readonly is shallow — nested objects and arrays are still mutable

entries.name: Pick<T, K>
entries.description: Constructs a type by picking a set of properties K from type T.

parameters.name: Keys
parameters.description: Union of property names to include.

entries.returns: New type with only specified properties

examples.title: Select specific fields

entries.name: Omit<T, K>
entries.description: Constructs a type by picking all properties from T and then removing the specified keys K. The inverse of Pick<T, K>.

parameters.name: Keys
parameters.description: Union of property names to exclude.

examples.title: Remove sensitive fields
Create insert type

useCases: Removing sensitive fields from response types

entries.name: Record<K, V>
entries.description: Constructs an object type whose property keys are K and whose property values are V. Useful for dictionaries and lookup maps.
entries.returns: Object type with keys K and values V

examples.title: String-to-number map
Enum-keyed lookup

entries.name: Exclude<T, U>
entries.description: Constructs a type by excluding from T all union members that are assignable to U.

parameters.name: ExcludedMembers
parameters.description: Types to exclude from the union.

entries.returns: Union type with specified members excluded

examples.title: Exclude from union
Remove null/undefined

entries.name: Extract<T, U>
entries.description: Constructs a type by extracting from T all union members that are assignable to U. The inverse of Exclude<T, U>.

parameters.name: Union
parameters.description: Types to keep in the union.

entries.returns: Union type with only matching members

examples.title: Extract string members
examples.code:
type Mixed = string | number | boolean | null;
type StringsOnly = Extract<Mixed, string>; // string

entries.name: NonNullable<T>
entries.description: Constructs a type by excluding null and undefined from T.

examples.title: Remove null/undefined

entries.name: ReturnType<T>
entries.description: Constructs a type consisting of the return type of function T. Useful for inferring types from function signatures.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The function type to extract the return type from.

entries.returns: The return type of the function

examples.title: Infer return type
Infer async return type

entries.name: Parameters<T>
entries.description: Constructs a tuple type from the parameter types of a function type T.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The function type to extract parameter types from.

examples.title: Extract parameter types

entries.name: Awaited<T>
entries.description: Extracts the type that a Promise resolves to, recursively unwrapping nested Promises.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: A Promise type or any type.

examples.title: Unwrap Promise type

entries.name: interface
entries.description: Defines the shape of an object. Interfaces are open (can be extended/merged), support declaration merging, and are the recommended way to type objects in TypeScript.

examples.title: Basic interface
Interface extension
Function interface

bestPractices: Prefer interface over type alias for object shapes when declaration merging may be useful
Use readonly for properties that should not change

entries.name: Generics
entries.description: Generics allow you to write reusable, type-safe code that works with any type. They are placeholders for types provided when the function, class, or interface is used.
entries.returns: Typed based on provided type argument

examples.title: Generic function
Generic with constraint
Generic API wrapper

entries.name: enum
entries.description: Enums define a set of named constants. TypeScript supports numeric (default) and string enums. Const enums are erased at compile time for better performance.

examples.title: String enum
Const enum (inlined at compile time)

bestPractices: Prefer const enum for better performance
Consider string enums for better debuggability (values match names)

entries.name: type (alias)
entries.description: Type aliases create a new name for any type, including primitives, unions, intersections, tuples, and complex types. More flexible than interface but does not support declaration merging.

examples.title: Union type
Intersection type
Conditional type

bestPractices: Use interface for object shapes, type alias for everything else (unions, intersections, primitives)

entries.name: Type Narrowing
entries.description: Narrowing refines a type to a more specific subtype using control flow analysis. TypeScript understands typeof, instanceof, in operator, discriminated unions, and custom type predicates.

examples.title: Discriminated union
Type predicate

entries.name: Decorators
entries.description: Decorators are a special kind of declaration that can be attached to a class, method, property, or parameter. They allow you to annotate and modify code at design time.

examples.title: Class decorator
Method decorator (logging)

bestPractices: Enable experimentalDecorators and emitDecoratorMetadata in tsconfig.json

entries.name: Modules & Imports
entries.description: TypeScript uses ES Module syntax for organizing code. Files with import/export are treated as modules. Supports named exports, default exports, re-exports, type-only imports, and dynamic imports.

examples.title: Named imports/exports
Type-only imports
Dynamic import

entries.name: Mapped Types
entries.description: Mapped types allow you to create new types by iterating over the keys of an existing type, transforming each property.

examples.title: Make all nullable
Getters/setters pattern

entries.name: Template Literal Types
entries.description: Template literal types build on string literal types to produce new string types via template literal syntax.

examples.title: Event name types
CSS property types
